edges.description: Two mechanisms are proposed for how losing FXYD2 reduces DCT magnesium reabsorption. One holds that the pump is destabilized and inactivated, so the cell cannot sustain the intracellular potassium that sets the apical membrane potential driving TRPM6 magnesium entry. The other holds that FXYD2 itself mediates basolateral magnesium exit, which the mutant cannot do. The step is not demonstrated in patient tissue.
intermediate_mechanisms: Na,K-ATPase destabilization with loss of apical driving force for TRPM6
loss of FXYD2-mediated basolateral magnesium extrusion

edges.description: The tubular defect is measured clinically as inappropriate urinary magnesium loss.
Continuing urinary magnesium loss lowers serum magnesium.
Low extracellular magnesium raises neuromuscular excitability.
Chronic magnesium deficiency reduces the activity of magnesium-dependent alkaline phosphatase, so inorganic pyrophosphate accumulates and calcium pyrophosphate crystals deposit in cartilage.
Neuromuscular hyperexcitability presents as muscle cramps.
Severe neuromuscular hyperexcitability presents as tetany.
Neuromuscular hyperexcitability can present as epileptic seizures.
The oocyte and MDCK assays show that G41R changes FXYD2 ion-handling and abolishes a basolateral magnesium current carried by wild-type FXYD2.
edges.limitations: Xenopus oocytes and canine MDCK cells are heterologous systems, not DCT cells, and the G41R gain-of-function cation current they report is one of two competing mechanisms and is not shown in patients.

nodes.description: FXYD2 forms oligomers, and G41R FXYD2 oligomerizes with itself and with wild-type FXYD2. When the two are co-expressed, processing of the wild-type protein (read out as artificial glycosylation) is reduced, which suggests the mutant holds wild-type subunits back from the plasma membrane. Haploinsufficiency is unlikely to explain the disease, because people lacking one FXYD2 copy have normal serum magnesium. A study of isolated transmembrane peptides found the opposite result for oligomerization, so the physical basis of the interference is not fully settled.

nodes.description: The gamma subunit is a regulatory subunit of the basolateral Na,K-ATPase in the DCT and other nephron segments. In the disease the pump loses its normal FXYD2 partner. Proximal tubular cells cultured from a patient's urine express less FXYD2 and raise FXYD2 and Na,K-ATPase less than control cells under hypertonic stress. Whether pump activity in the DCT ends up lower or higher is debated, because FXYD2 both inhibits the pump kinetically and stabilizes it.

nodes.description: The distal convoluted tubule sets final urinary magnesium, and its transcellular reabsorption falls. Because more distal segments are largely impermeable to magnesium, the DCT defect is not compensated and magnesium is lost in the urine. Urinary calcium is low, which distinguishes this disorder from the hypercalciuric forms of renal magnesium wasting.
